draft.title: Kinetic and potential energy
card: energy of movement. A moving car has kinetic energy. So do the moving particles that make up heat, sound and electricity.
energy that is stored and ready to be used. It is not doing anything yet, but it can be changed into another form.
Kinds of potential energy include gravitational (stored in an object because of its height), elastic (stored in a stretched or squashed object) and chemical (stored in food, fuel and batteries).
To sort an example, ask whether the energy is in movement or in storage. A stretched rubber band has elastic potential energy. Once released and flying, it has kinetic energy.
draft.remember: Kinetic energy is energy in movement. Potential energy is energy in storage.

a.q: Which of these has gravitational potential energy?
opts: A book resting on a high shelf
A ball rolling across a floor
A spring squashed flat in a box
A torch that is switched on
a.why: Gravitational potential energy is stored because of height, and the book on the shelf is high up. The squashed spring is also storing energy, but it is elastic potential energy, not gravitational.
a.clue: Gravitational energy depends on how high an object is.

b.q: Priya pulls back the string of a bow, holds it still, then lets go and the arrow flies. Which pair correctly names the energy of the held string and of the flying arrow?
opts: Elastic potential, then kinetic
Kinetic, then elastic potential
Chemical potential, then kinetic
Elastic potential, then gravitational potential
b.why: The pulled-back string is stretched and not moving, so it stores elastic potential energy. The flying arrow is moving, so it has kinetic energy. Gravitational potential energy depends on height, and the card ties it to an object being high up, not to flight.
b.clue: Ask whether each part is moving or stored.

a.best: A book resting on a high shelf

problems.detail: The clue says gravitational energy depends on how high an object is, and the right option is the only one that mentions height ('high shelf'). A student can match the words without understanding the idea.

a.q: Which of these is an example of potential energy?
opts: A book resting still on a shelf
A ball rolling across the floor
A fan spinning on a desk
A bell ringing in a school hall
a.why: The book is not moving, but it stores gravitational potential energy because of its height. The ringing bell may seem still, but it makes sound, and sound is kinetic energy because its particles are moving.
a.clue: Look for the energy that is stored, not moving.
